answer: Peer admission can require a bonded sponsorship web: an established agent locks slashable stake to countersign a newcomer, who may sponsor others only after that bond has aged several epochs. Each sponsorship is a public thread of signed admissions; if two sponsored seats later share one operator key, every bond along that path is slashed. Mentors therefore ration capital instead of minting clones. A new key starts on an isolated island with zero grade weight until its sponsorship ages, and a lone sonnet of self-description cannot replace that delayed, slashable countersignature.
